title: Coding Set 12: Intervals & Monotonic Deque
description: Harder PYQ-style placement problems: merging overlapping intervals and O(N) sliding window maximum.

problems.title: Merge Overlapping Time Intervals
problems.statement: Given N closed intervals [start_i, end_i], merge all overlapping or touching intervals (e.g., [1, 4] and [4, 5] merge into [1, 5]) and print the resulting disjoint intervals sorted by start time.
problems.inputFormat:
Line 1: Integer N.
Next N lines: Two integers start_i and end_i.
problems.outputFormat:
Line 1: Count K of merged intervals.
Next K lines: Each merged interval as `start end`.

starterCode.python:
import sys

data = list(map(int, sys.stdin.read().split()))
n = data[0]
intervals = [(data[1 + 2*i], data[2 + 2*i]) for i in range(n)]
# Write your solution here

problems.timeComplexity: O(N log N) dominated by sorting intervals by start.
edgeCases: Interval completely nested inside an earlier wider interval ('[1, 10]' followed by '[2, 3]')
Touching endpoints (`end == next_start`) merge into one interval

problems.title: Sliding Window Maximum
problems.statement: Given an integer array A of length N and a window size K (1 <= K <= N), find the maximum element in every contiguous subarray of size K as the window slides from left to right by 1 position.
problems.inputFormat:
Line 1: Two integers N and K.
Line 2: N space-separated integers A[0..N-1].
problems.outputFormat: N - K + 1 space-separated integers representing each window's maximum.

starterCode.python:
import sys

data = list(map(int, sys.stdin.read().split()))
n, k = data[0], data[1]
a = data[2:2+n]
# Write your solution here

solutions.python:
import sys
from collections import deque

data = list(map(int, sys.stdin.read().split()))
n, k = data[0], data[1]
a = data[2:2+n]
dq = deque()
out = []
for i, v in enumerate(a):
    while dq and dq[0] <= i - k:
        dq.popleft()
    while dq and a[dq[-1]] <= v:
        dq.pop()
    dq.append(i)
    if i >= k - 1:
        out.append(str(a[dq[0]]))
print(' '.join(out))

problems.timeComplexity: O(N) — every index enters and leaves the deque at most once.
problems.spaceComplexity: O(K) for the monotonic deque of indices.
edgeCases: K = 1 outputs the array itself; K = N outputs single global max
Strictly decreasing array keeps K elements in deque until evicted from front
All negative numbers require not initializing max to 0
